vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability is in the _transferBothExcluded function. When both sender and recipient are excluded from rewards, the function subtracts tAmount from _tOwned[sender] and adds tTransferAmount to _tOwned[recipient]. However, if these addresses were never properly initialized in the _tOwned mapping (i.e., they were excluded but had zero _rOwned balance when excluded), their _tOwned entries might be uninitialized storage pointers. This could lead to incorrect token accounting, potentially allowing fee evasion or manipulation of swapAndLiquify to drain BNB from the contract.
attack_strategy: 1. Get attacker address excluded from rewards via owner call. 2. Ensure attacker has some tokens. 3. Transfer tokens to another excluded address (like contract itself or owner) to trigger _transferBothExcluded path. 4. Exploit the uninitialized storage pointer to manipulate token balances and potentially trigger swapAndLiquify in a way that benefits the attacker.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Impersonate the owner to call excludeFromReward on attacker address. 2. Get some JizzJet tokens to the attacker. 3. Make sure the contract has accumulated enough tokens to trigger swapAndLiquify (numTokensSellToAddToLiquidity threshold). 4. Transfer tokens from attacker (excluded) to another excluded address (like contract address) to trigger _transferBothExcluded. 5. The uninitialized storage pointer might cause incorrect fee calculations or balance updates, potentially allowing the attacker to receive more tokens or BNB than expected.
